history.dynasty: Pandyas (12th century core); expanded by the Setupatis of Ramanathapuram - Dalavai Setupati built part of the eastern gopuram (17th century), Muthuramalinga Setupati built the third corridor 'Chokkatan Mandapam' (ruled 1763-1795)
history.summary: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, a Char Dham pilgrimage site and a Paadal Petra Sthalam on Rameswaram island. Legend: Rama worshipped Shiva here before crossing to Lanka; the lingam was made by Sita (Ramalingam), while Hanuman brought the Vishwalingam from Kailasha - the Vishwalingam is worshipped first even today, and a scar on the lingam is said to be Hanuman's tail mark. Famed for the world's longest temple corridors (about 3,850 ft total, ~1,212 pillars, 53-m rajagopuram) and 22 theerthams (holy water bodies, including Agni Theertham by the sea) where devotees bathe before darshan. Administered by the HRCE Department.

name: Ramanathaswamy Temple
town_description: The principal temple town on Rameswaram island (Pamban island) in Ramanathapuram district, about 600 km from Chennai, reached by the Pamban road/rail bridge from the mainland.
tradition: Shaivite (Jyotirlinga, Char Dham, Paadal Petra Sthalam)

travel.airport: Madurai airport is the nearest major airport (distance verify)
travel.railway: Rameswaram railway station, connected via the Pamban bridge
travel.road: Well connected by road from Madurai (~170 km, verify) and Ramanathapuram across the Pamban bridge

visitor_information.best_time: October to April; avoid the peak summer heat
visitor_information.opening_hours: Typically morning and evening sessions with a midday break (commonly cited 5:00/6:00 a.m.-1:00 p.m., 3:00-9:00 p.m. - verify current timings)
